take_homes: Count how much of what was freely available people actually used. The folder-citing ratio is the right adoption metric, so don't promise the board a percentage before measuring it.
Agents reading each other's work invent sources unless every claim names its file. Make them cite, and check the citation myself.
A plan should say what evidence would make us drop it. I'll ask that of any AI proposal I'm shown.

monday.move: Ask my controller to try the month-end variance commentary with an agent once, on redacted data, with every claim citing its source file, and have them write down the time spent.
monday.who: my controller, with me reviewing the output
monday.when: the month-end close, a week from Monday
monday.stop_condition: If citations are missing or the time saved is not clearly more than the time spent checking, drop it.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data, so the data stays redacted until it does.

misconception.why: The line about company knowledge staying flat while models improve suggests a licence alone won't build capability. It came as one sentence with no figure, so I'm only partly convinced and still think of AI as something you buy.

one_line: Three good ideas (count the folders, make agents cite, name what would change your mind) wrapped in 70 minutes of agents talking to agents, with no cost, payback or risk number anywhere.
